test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 18 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A shopkeeper fixes the marked price of an item 52% above its cost price. What percentage of discount on the marked price should be allowed to gain 14%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the relationship: **MP ÷ CP = (100 + P%) ÷ (100 − D%)**.

Given: **MP = 152** (if CP = 100) and **Profit = 14%**.

152 ÷ 100 = (100 + 14) ÷ (100 − D).

152 ÷ 100 = 114 ÷ (100 − D) ⇒ 100 − D = (114 × 100) ÷ 152.

100 − D = 75 ⇒ **D = 25%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Marked Price (MP) is 52% above Cost Price (CP), Profit = 14%.

**Formulas:** SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100 | Discount% = (MP − SP) ÷ MP × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/df22b5d8dc73c196aca7beabf468c4c750c18e47492fb0140387443eb308e390.png] 

⇒ Let **Cost Price (CP)** = 100.

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 52% of 100 = 152.

⇒ Desired **Profit** = 14%, so **Selling Price (SP)** = 100 + 14 = 114.

⇒ **Discount Amount** = MP − SP = 152 − 114 = 38.

⇒ **Discount%** = (38 ÷ 152) × 100 = 1/4 × 100 = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between CP, MP, Profit and Discount

The ratio of MP to CP is always constant for a given profit and discount: **MP/CP = (100 + Gain%) / (100 − Discount%)**.

Marked Price

It is the price displayed on the label of an item, also known as the **List Price**.</p
